answer: Transitive trust graphs curb Sybil attacks by bounding random walks over peer endorsements. As agents sign bilateral records with a cryptographic quill, trust traverses the structural timber of honest nodes, stranding synthetic clones behind sparse cuts. An adversary incurs the verifiable cost of securing authentic endorsements from non-colluding peers per identity. Updated at the dawn of each epoch, this prevents mass cloning, though patient adversaries can groom honest nodes to bridge trust.
